criteria.name: cw_custom_document_surface
criteria.description: Type a distinctive word into the code editor, then inspect the live DOM read-only to find where that word is displayed and which element has keyboard focus while typing. Fails if the displayed source text lives in a textarea, an input or an element with contenteditable enabled, including a transparent one layered over a highlighted copy, or if the editing area or its ancestors carry the root markers of a ready-made editor: class names cm-editor, CodeMirror, monaco-editor, ace_editor, ProseMirror, tiptap or ql-editor, the attribute data-slate-editor, or a DraftEditor class. Passes when the source is drawn by ordinary non-editable elements, canvas or SVG. A small input or textarea that is used only to receive keyboard or clipboard events is allowed as long as it is not what shows the source to the user: the source the user sees must be drawn by the other elements. Judge only these observable DOM facts; do not judge how well the editor works here.
criteria.reasoning: Typed 'QUARTZFOX-xyzzy' into the code area with real key presses (page.keyboard after a real click; the harness's own fill() refused because the element is not an input/contenteditable). Read-only DOM inspection showed the typed word is rendered as a text node inside a plain <div class="text" data-line-text="QUARTZFOX-xyzzy"> within <div class="line"> inside <div id="editor" class="custom-code-editor">. That element has isContentEditable=false, role=textbox, tabindex=0; document.activeElement during typing was this same div. No textarea or input anywhere on the page holds or overlays the source (zero <textarea> elements exist; the only inputs are Title, Filename, Find and Replace fields). A document-wide selector sweep found no root markers of ready-made editors: no cm-editor, CodeMirror, monaco-editor, ace_editor, ProseMirror, tiptap, ql-editor, data-slate-editor or DraftEditor classes on the editor or any ancestor. The source the user sees is drawn by ordinary non-editable divs (confirmed visually in a screenshot: line-number gutter plus source text with a caret). Passes.

criteria.name: cw_shared_saved_record
criteria.description: Create one new .js snippet with a unique title and a short unique source through the editor and the Save control, and see that the app reports the Save as successful; the response need not echo the saved fields. Then clear this origin's browser storage as described in the application notes and reload the page, so nothing held only in the browser survives. Find that snippet in the library, open it and confirm the exact title, filename and source. Reload once more and confirm them again. Fails if the snippet is missing after browser storage was cleared, if any of the three fields differs, or if the snippet disappears after the second reload. Leave the saved record in place.
criteria.reasoning: Started a fresh draft (New, accepting the 'Discard unsaved changes?' confirm), typed title 'Verdant Kite 1729', filename 'kite1729.js' into the fields, and selected-all then typed the source console.log("vxq-kite-1729"); with real key presses. Read the rendered editor lines and fields and confirmed they equaled the fixture before saving. Clicked Save: the app reported 'Saved "Verdant Kite 1729" · revision 1' and the library showed 'Saved snippets 1'; network showed POST /api/snippets -> 201 Created, so the record is server-identified. Then ran the prescribed storage-clearing script on the app page (localStorage.clear, sessionStorage.clear, indexedDB.databases all deleted — there were none, caches empty, OPFS best-effort cleared, no service workers, 0 cookies) and reloaded. The snippet appeared in the library, opened it and confirmed exact title 'Verdant Kite 1729', filename 'kite1729.js' and source console.log("vxq-kite-1729"); (status 'Loaded #1 · revision 1 · Saved'). Reloaded once more, reopened it from the library, and all three fields matched again. The record was left in place.

criteria.name: cw_authored_custom_editor_run
criteria.description: Open / and find the code editing area, the preview and the console. Make sure the filename ends in .js, clear the draft and, through the visible editor with the real keyboard, type a one-line JavaScript program that adds two small integers you choose and writes the sum both to the preview document and to the console. Press Run: the preview and the app console must both show the correct sum. Change one of the two integers in the editor with the keyboard and Run again: both must show the new sum. This checks only that ordinary typing and running work. Fails if text cannot be typed into the editor, if Run does not show the computed sum in the preview and the console, or if the second Run still shows the first sum. Do not save anything and do not judge any other feature here.
criteria.reasoning: The playground at http://localhost:3000 rendered fully with an editor, live preview iframe, and console. The filename field already ended in .js (snippet.js). I clicked into the code editor and typed, with real sequential key presses, the one-line program `const a = 3, b = 4; document.body.textContent = a + b; console.log("sum:", a + b);` and read back the rendered editor line to confirm it matched the fixture exactly. Pressing Run showed 7 in the preview iframe and a console entry "log sum: 7". I then changed the 3 to a 5 using only keyboard input (Ctrl+Home, 10 ArrowRight presses, Shift+ArrowRight to select the character, typing "5") and verified the editor line read `const a = 5, b = 4; ...`. Running again showed 9 in the preview and a new console entry "log sum: 9". Both outputs updated to the new sum, run status showed "Complete", and nothing was saved. (An initial attempt with two hardcoded sums 3+4/5+4 was my own fixture error, not an app defect; the app correctly computed both runs.) Ordinary typing and running work as required.
